Sofia (sec-eng): Heads up — after the RBAC change we rolled to restrict encrypt:Decrypt on the region-keystore role, we're seeing intermittent TLS handshakes fail for service-to-service traffic inside the private VPC.
James (infra): Can you paste a sample error?
Sofia (sec-eng): Sure — stacktrace from proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-22T14:12:03Z proxy-1 tls_handshake.go:217 ERROR failed to unwrap key: kms:AccessDeniedException keyId=projects/.... region-keystore
caused_by: RPC error: remote handshake aborted
```
Li (sre): That matches a spike I saw — connection attempts from svc-a -> svc-b returned 502s for ~30s around 14:12. Good news: not global.
Sofia (sec-eng): My hypothesis: RBAC tightened the role used by the rotator, and when a node tried to fetch the intermediate chain it couldn't decrypt the wrapped key. Fallback path should let the proxy use cached KV, but cache TTL was low.
James (infra): Did AuditBot capture the KMS denies? @AuditBot can you confirm?
AuditBot: Alert ID #A-20260322-77: 24 KMS:Decrypt DENY events for principal service-account/region-keystore-role between 2026-03-22T14:11:50Z and 2026-03-22T14:12:20Z. Full log pushed to /logs/security/kms-deny/2026-03-22/A-20260322-77.json
Li (sre): Ok that correlates. Two immediate asks: 1) temporary mitigation to restore traffic, 2) longer-term fix so config drift doesn't break handshakes.
Sofia (sec-eng): Mitigation proposal: add a narrow IAM allow for `service-account/proxy-fanout` to `kms:Decrypt` for the specific key alias for 30 minutes, and widen cache TTL to 5m. Then revert IAM. Thoughts?
James (infra): +1 for quick rollback window. Do we have an auditable jumpbox flow to do the IAM change? I want it done via infra pipeline (not console).
Li (sre): I can run the infra change through the emergency job: `./infra/run-iam-patch --role region-keystore-role --grant \"service-account:proxy-fanout:kms:Decrypt\" --duration 30m` — it emits a changelog entry.
Sofia (sec-eng): Perfect. While that's happening, we should also ingest the deny events into the security audit pipeline. Add a tag on the IAM patch: `audit:incident=handshake-2026-03-22`
James (infra): DeployBot, kick off the IAM patch job please.
DeployBot: Started job j-1147 by user Li (sre). Patch command: `./infra/run-iam-patch --role region-keystore-role --grant \"service-account:proxy-fanout:kms:Decrypt\" --duration 30m --tag handshake-2026-03-22`. Job logs: /ci/jobs/j-1147/logs
Li (sre): Patch applied, cache TTL bumped to 5m on proxies via canary group 1/6. Monitoring dashboards updated.
Sofia (sec-eng): Can we confirm handshakes recovered? Any remaining 502s?
Li (sre): Dashboards show error rate back to baseline within 40s of the patch. No continuing denies after regrant.
James (infra): Next steps (post-mitigation): 1) Postmortem with timeline and root cause, 2) update RBAC rollout playbook to include KMS-boundary checks, 3) modify rotator to fall back gracefully when decrypt fails (serve cached chain longer + circuit-breaker).
Sofia (sec-eng): I'll own the PM for the postmortem. Quick checklist for the write-up: list of principals changed, KMS log excerpts, proxy cache TTLs, and canary rollout matrix. Also want to add automated tests that simulate KMS Deny events during CI.
AuditBot: Noted. I'll snapshot the KMS deny dataset and attach to ticket SEC-4621.
James (infra): Li, please open infra PR that adds an IAM preflight check into our RBAC deploy pipeline: query KMS with the service principal before committing. Sample check (one-liner):
```bash
aws kms test-invoke --key-id alias/region-keystore --principal arn:aws:iam::111111:role/service-account/proxy-fanout || exit 1
```
Li (sre): Will do. Also adding an observability assertion to fail rollouts if KMS deny rate > 0 for 1m in canary.
Sofia (sec-eng): Thanks everyone. After the postmortem we'll schedule a cross-team runbook review (sec + infra + sre) and add the audit log retention rule for KMS denies to 90 days.
James (infra): SGTM. :thumbsup:
Li (sre): Closing loop — I'll link the incident ticket once PR + postmortem exist.
Sofia (sec-eng): Closing here for now. If anything else pops up ping me directly. :lock:
